title: Unlocking rapid room-temperature crystallization of MOF-808 through green synthesis for high-performance tartrazine and Congo red dye adsorption
content: The current work presents a distinctive green strategy for the rapid room-temperature crystallization of pristine MOF-808, overcoming the conventional reliance on toxic organic solvents, elevated temperatures, and prolonged synthesis times. MOF-808 was directly assembled in an aqueous formic acid medium at ambient temperature, with an optimum condition identified as a total reaction volume of 10 mL and an HCOOH/H2O ratio of 1 : 4, yielding well-defined, relatively small and uniformly distributed crystals with limited agglomeration and high crystalline ordering. The optimized MOF-808 exhibited a high BET surface area of 1827.34 m2 g−1, a micropore area of 928.71 m2 g−1, and an average pore diameter of 1.89 nm. Under optimal adsorption conditions (pH 7, 0.02 g adsorbent, 30 °C, and 50 min), removal efficiencies reached 99.64% for Congo Red (CR) and 99.74% for Tartrazine (TA), while Langmuir maximum capacities were 847.45 and 434.78 mg g−1, respectively. The adsorption was rapid, spontaneous, and exothermic, involving synergistic electrostatic attraction, π–π interactions, hydrogen bonding, and possible Zr–O coordination. MOF-808 retained substantial activity after four regeneration cycles, with CR and TA removal efficiencies of 73.69 and 85.45%, respectively. Importantly, a mung bean (Vigna radiata) germination assay demonstrated that MOF-808 treatment substantially alleviated the inhibitory effects of CR/TA on seed germination and seedling development, highlighting its potential for sustainable dye remediation beyond conventional concentration-based performance assessment.
